chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
For everything is a sanctity, and the sanctity of the animals is in their faces.
ai.seo_question: What is the sanctity of animals in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the universal principle of 'hurmah' (sanctity) applicable to all entities, extending it specifically to animals. The emphasis on the 'face' (wajh) as the locus of this sanctity reflects the Shia juristic understanding of preserving the inherent dignity of living creatures, serving as a foundational basis for rules regarding animal slaughter and avoiding unnecessary harm. This hadith underscores the ethical dimension of creation in Shia thought, where respect for the physical integrity of animals is a religious obligation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘For everything is a sanctity, and a sanctity of the animals is in their faces’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Everything has honor. The honor of animals is in their faces.’”
